questions.text: Which of the following is an efficient method of cache updating?
questions.solution:
In multiprocessor caches, snoopy protocols watch the bus and update or invalidate copies as writes happen, keeping caches coherent efficiently.

Answer: Snoopy writes

questions.text:
A computer which issues instructions in order, has only 2 registers and 3 opcodes ADD, SUB and MOV. Consider 2 different implementations of the following basic block :
[latex]\begin{array}{l|l} \text { Case } 1 & \text { Case } 2 \\ \hline t 1=a+b ; & t 2=c+d \\ t 2=c+d ; & t 3=e-t 2 \\ t 3=e-t 2 ; & t 1=a+b \\ t 4=t 1-t 2 ; & t 4=t 1-t 2 \end{array}[/latex]
Assume that all operands are initially in memory. Final value of computation also has to reside in memory. Which one is better in terms of memory accesses and by how many MOV instructions?
questions.solution:
With only 2 registers:
- Case 1: t1 and t2 fill both registers, but t3 = e [latex]-[/latex] t2 needs a register for e, so t1 must be stored to memory (MOV) and later loaded back for t4 (MOV) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 extra MOVs.
- Case 2: compute t2, then t3 (t2 stays in a register), then t1 in the freed register, then t4 = t1 [latex]-[/latex] t2. No spilling is needed.

Case 2 saves 2 MOV instructions (memory accesses).

Answer: Case 2, 2

questions.text: A stack organized computer is characterised by instructions with
questions.solution:
A stack machine takes operands from the top of the stack, so instructions like ADD need no address field: zero-address instructions.

Answer: zero addressing

questions.text: Consider a 32- bit processor which supports 70 instructions. Each instruction is 32 bit long and has 4 fields namely opcode, two register identifiers and an immediate operand of unsigned integer type. Maximum value of the immediate operand that can be supported by the processor is 8191. How many registers the processor has?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Immediate max 8191 = [latex]2^{13}-1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 13 bits.
- 70 instructions [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7-bit opcode.
- Remaining for two register fields: 32 [latex]-[/latex] 13 [latex]-[/latex] 7 = 12 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 bits each.

Registers = [latex]2^6=64[/latex]

Answer: 64

questions.text: Consider a 5- segment pipeline with a clock cycle time 20 ns in each sub operation. Find out the approximate speed-up ratio between pipelined and non-pipelined system to execute 100 instructions. (if an average, every five cycles, a bubble due to data hazard has to be introduced in the pipeline)
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Non-pipelined: 100 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 20 ns = 10000 ns.
- Pipelined: 5 + 99 = 104 cycles, plus one bubble every 5 instructions ([latex]\approx[/latex] 20 bubbles) = 124 cycles [latex]\times[/latex] 20 ns = 2480 ns.

Speedup = 10000 / 2480 [latex]\approx[/latex] 4.03

Answer: 4.03
